In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NJL model with the mean vector field is capable of describing the nuclear matter properties as well as the nuclear medium effects in the structure functions of a nucleon.
the EMC effect is a genuine nuclear effect, and is not a quark effect.

a description of the EMC effect in terms of a modification of the quark distribution in the nucleon, which is consistent with the equation of state, is possible, but the required modifications of the quark distributions are rather small and the effect is dominated by the mean vector field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EMC effect is a consequence of the mean vector meson field, which is a result of a self‐consistent treatment of the NJL model in the medium.
the EMC effect is a manifestation of the change of the quark momentum distribution in the nuclear medium.
the EMC effect can be understood in terms of the NJL model with a proper inclusion of the mean vector potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NJL model, which is a simple model of QCD, provides a consistent description of nuclear matter and the EMC effect.
the EMC effect is not just a matter of the nuclear mean field, but also a consequence of the modification of the quark wave functions in nuclear matter, which can be described in the NJL framework.
, in the framework we use, it is not necessary to introduce any nonlocal effects to describe the structure function in nuclear matter.
